name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +21 partisan lean
Jasmine Clark's large fundraising and outside support edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 97%
Open seat with no polling available
model.rationale: The district's +21 Democratic lean and a favorable national environment make this a Safe D seat even without an incumbent on the ballot. Clark has raised over $1.6 million with $4.2 million in outside support and no opposition spending, while Chavez reports no fundraising, and markets price a Democratic win at 97%.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a surge of outside spending against Clark would be the main signal to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 13th District is a heavily Democratic Atlanta-area seat with a +21 Democratic partisan lean, and David Scott's party holds it comfortably. With Everton Blair not on the ballot, Democrat Jasmine Clark enters the general election as the clear favorite. She has raised about $1.6 million and benefits from roughly $4.2 million in outside support, with no recorded spending against her.

Republican Jonathan Chavez has no reported fundraising or cash on hand, and no independent polls of the race are available. Prediction markets give the Democratic candidate about a 97% chance of winning. The combination of district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing points to a comfortable Democratic hold in the mid-twenties margin range.
